line: - **one-board** Keep one board page for the whole project that shows at a glance where it stands and what each line of work is doing.
note: The second half of the old rule (few things, shown large, for a screen read from a few steps away) is layout and stays with the template.

line: - **board-owns-nothing** The board only reads the logs: no state, no log changed from it; whether to commit it is the project's call.
note: board-log#19 adds: nothing becomes true because it is on the board; it goes into the board-writing long file. The reason for not committing it (delete it and write it again, every fact is the same; only the time differs) also goes there.

lines: - **board-writer** A cheap model writes scrum/ScrumBoard.html when the PO wants to look or a log changed.
- **board-rules** What the board reads, the data it holds, how to copy and check it: read the long file before writing one. → long/board-writing.md
note: The long file says who writes it: a fresh subagent told to read the board rules and the template, or a standing helper session of the PO's (the wording of that helper waits for the secretary role of PBI-86 / Sprint 27).

pending.board-writer: Sprint 27: the Supporter writes the board. Rewrite the line (and the 'who writes it' paragraph of the board-writing long file) when 27 is merged.

note: The log paths, the rule that a Sprint or design open on another branch counts (read as committed there; source `branch <name> @ <commit>`), the working-copy rule and the newest-commit rule go into the long file word for word. My override of the verifiers: they pointed at the board check script, which is not in the plugin.
What to take from each log (six bullets) goes into the long file, convention numbers replaced by handles. My override of the verifiers, as for board-log#4.

Maps: the product log's map is the Mermaid diagram in section 2.2, a design log's the one in its 2.1; a node's label is the text inside the quotation marks of the three bracket forms; arrows and their labels are not nodes.

where_else: plugins/ideo-scrum/skills/scrum-kernel/conventions/scrum-board-template.html draws the overview (flow, lighting, colours); the layout reasons are in the design archive of the board.

note: Only the kept part goes into the long file: a design card has its own solution section that shows what was chosen and how it is used, even without a storyboard, or says that none is chosen; it invents no storyboard. The three-layer card layout stays with the template.

One or two sentences in the long file: the page works out a Sprint's name, short names, counts, order and links itself, so none of that is written in the data. My override of the verifiers' delete: that sentence is only here.

A card links to its log relative to scrum/ only when its source is the working copy; a log only on another branch shows the branch and the commit, so no link is dead; every card's foot starts with its folder's name.
